title: GPT-SoVITS webui -- T1059 Gradio textbox shell=True command injection
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Detection for CVE-2026-63766 (CVSS 9.3 CRITICAL), affecting GPT-SoVITS
through version 20250606v2pro.

`webui.py`'s ASR, slice, denoise, and uvr5 handlers (the ASR path,
approximately lines 376-395) build shell command strings by directly
interpolating Gradio textbox values -- e.g.
`cmd = '"%s" -s tools/asr/funasr/funasr_asr.py -i "%s" -o "%s" ...' %
(python_exec, asr_inp_dir, asr_opt_dir)` -- and execute them with
`Popen(cmd, shell=True)`. The project's own sanitization helper,
`clean_path()` (`tools/my_utils.py`, near line 39), strips only
whitespace and quote characters; it does not remove shell
metacharacters (`;`, `` ` ``, `$()`), so an attacker who can reach the
webui (no authentication by default) can supply a crafted path value
such as `"; touch /tmp/pwned; "` to break out of the intended quoted
argument and run an arbitrary trailing command as the server process
user -- the same underlying flaw repeats across all four affected
handlers.

Detection logic flags the resulting host-level artifact: a `Popen`/
shell child process spawned as a descendant of the GPT-SoVITS webui
process whose command line contains a shell metacharacter immediately
following a quoted path-like argument -- the specific
`"<path>" ... "; <injected>"` construction `clean_path()`'s incomplete
filtering makes possible.

Aggregated from 1 first-party GitHub issue with maintainer/community
discussion (RVC-Boss/GPT-SoVITS, via VulnCheck's corroborating
write-up), quoting the vulnerable code and confirming the injection
behavior.
